full_judgment:
90. PW 8 Abdul Zahir was then a Deputy Jailor working at the Central Jail, Dhaka from 1974-77 who deposed that while he was sleeping at his residence at 4-00 AM one Jail guard informed him that the IG (Prisons), DIG (Prisons) and the Jailor had arrived at the office; he also heard the sounds of alarm inside the Jail so he rushed to his office after dressing and upon reaching there he was informed that the Jailor was inside the Jail; then he wanted to go to the office of the DIG (Prisons) but the Orderly (আর্দালী)resisted him to enter into, informing him that the IG (Prisons) and the DIG (Prisons) were engrossed with army personnel inside the office then he returned to his own office and had found some other colleagues were sitting there; 15/20 minutes after he was informed that the Jailor had returned back to his office so he then went to the office of the Jailor and wanted to know why he had been called in; then the Jailor informed him to wait for some time thereafter he found the DIG (Prisons) and the Jailor along with 5 army personnel were proceeding towards the new Jail so he also followed them, upon entering inside, he heard sounds of gun shots so he took shelter in the back side of a tin shed house; some time after, 5 army personnel along with IG (Prisons), DIG (Prisons) and the Jailor got out from the Jail thereafter he got the information that the 4 leaders had been killed. Thereafter, on 5-11-1975 the dead bodies of the 4 leaders were handed over to their respective relations. This witness also proved the gate register where his name is there as Exhibit (7/2). He also proved Exhibit 8(3) his signature available at page 144 of Exhibit 8. This witness during cross-examination admitted that Exhibits 7 and 8 do not contain any proof as to whether those are the documents belonging to the Central Jail, Dhaka. He also admitted that the signature available at page 118 of Exhibit 7 is not by his own hands. He also admitted that official seal of Central Jail was not there in Exhibit 7. He also admitted that he was examined by the Investigating Officer on 24-8-96. He also denied his liability under section 302 of the Penal Code in the killing of 4 national leaders. This witness also admitted in his deposition to the effect that : 

 This piece of evidence lends support to the defence version of the case and in a position like this the case of Muslimuddin vs State reported in 38 DLR (AD) 311 may be referred to wherefrom we find that the principle laid down in that case is that the fundamental principle of a criminal trial is that the accused shall be presumed innocent and that he is not required to adduce evidence to prove his innocence, but the entire burden of proof of his guilt lies on the prosecution alone and till that time the presumption of innocence continues, whether the case is before the trial Court or at higher forums..........................................................................................In a criminal case it is the duty of the Court to review the entire evidence that has been produced by the prosecution and the defence, if after an examination of the whole evidence, the Court is of opinion that there is reasonable possibility that the defence put forward by the accused might be true, it is clear that such a view reacts on the whole prosecution case. In these circumstances the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt, not as a matter of grace but as of right, because the prosecution has not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
